document.title: The Harakat-ul-Ansar - The Pakistan Dimension [Excised] (Karachi 01617)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Secret] Report on the Kashmiri militant group Harakat-ul-Ansar. Many of its activists are Afghan war veterans who fought with Maulana Jalaluddin Haqqani in Paktia. A significant portion of the membership is non-Pakistani, including veterans from Algeria, Tunisia, Sudan, Egypt and elsewhere. Three sources say the membership also includes a small number of American Muslims, with estimates ranging from six to sixteen.

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Afghan mujahideen commander in Paktia; Afghan war veterans of HuA reportedly fought with him and former mujahideen associated with him conduct HuA training

mentions.quote: VETERANS OF THE AFGHAN WAR WHO FOUGHT ALONG WITH MAULANA JALAUDDIN HAQQANI IN PAKTIA PROVINCE
BY FORMER AFGHAN MUJAHIDEEN; ASSOCIATED WITH MAULANA HAQQANT.

persons.name: Fazil ur-Rehman Khalil
persons.role: Reported leader of Harakat ul Ansar (named by two sources)

mentions.quote: THE NAME GIVEN BY TWO SOURCES AS THE LEADER OF HARAKAT IS FAZIL UR~REHMAN KHALIL.
CAME TO KARACHI IN THE AFTERMATH OF THE FEBRUARY 5 SHOOTINGS TO OFFER CONDOLENCES TO FAMILIES OF THE VICTIMS.
A MAULANA FAROOQ KASHMIRI IS THE LEADER OF HUA.

persons.name: Pir Wijahad Ali
persons.role: Pakistani pir in Rawalpindi with reported American Muslim following, linked to HuA membership

mentions.quote: ONE SOURCE NAMED A PIR WIJAHAD ALI IN RAWALPINDI AS THE PIR WITH AN AMERICAN FOLLOWING.

organizations.name: Harakat ul Ansar
aliases: Movement of Friends or Supporters of the Prophet
organizations.notes: Deobandi Sunni group, 2,000-10,000 activists, many foreign Afghan war veterans; fights in Kashmir, presence in Chechnya, Bosnia, Philippines, Burma; trains near Miran Shah and across border; raises funds privately; kidnapped two British citizens in Kashmir in 1994; no threat to the US indicated.

organizations.name: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI/F)
organizations.notes: Reported sponsor of HuA; uses group for political and financial support.

organizations.name: Sipah-e-Sahaba Pakistan
organizations.notes: Reported links with HuA; focused on domestic scene.

organizations.name: Tablighi Jamaat
organizations.notes: Non-political missionary organization from which original HuA activists reportedly came.

events.description: Violence in Karachi killed 23; drive-by shooting of HuA fundraising pavilion in Liaquatabad
Shooting of two U.S. Consulate employees in Karachi
HuA kidnapped two British citizens in Indian-controlled Kashmir
Cable sent by AMCONSUL Karachi to State Department
HUA begins participation in Kashmir militancy (at least since).
HUA kidnapped two British citizens in Indian-controlled Kashmir (last spring).
Violence in Karachi killed 23; drive-by shooting hit HUA fundraising pavilion in Liaquatabad.
HUA ran five fundraising pavilions across Karachi for Kashmir jihad.
Shooting of two U.S. Consulate employees in Karachi.
Khalil visited Karachi to offer condolences after the Feb 5 shootings.
HUA first organized in central Punjab to assist Afghan mujahideen.
U.S. Consulate Karachi sends cable on HUA's Pakistan dimension.
Harakat ul Ansar reportedly first organized in central Punjab to assist mujahideen in Afghanistan.
Drive-by shootings in Karachi linked to a Harakat fund-raising effort; Khalil later visited Karachi to offer condolences to the victims' families.
Khalil reportedly came to Karachi after the February 5 shootings to offer condolences.
A source told the Consulate that Harakat has publicly solicited donations in various Pakistani cities.
U.S. Consulate Karachi sent the cable, coordinated with Embassy Islamabad.

key_claims: HuA is a Deobandi Sunni group of 2,000-10,000 activists, many foreign Afghan war veterans.
HuA training camps are west of Miran Shah and across the border in Afghanistan, run by former mujahideen associated with Jalaluddin Haqqani.
Many HuA members fought with Haqqani in Paktia.
JUI/F reportedly sponsors HuA and has links with SSP.
HuA raises substantial private funds in Pakistan, Egypt, Algeria, Sudan and from Gujarati Muslims in London.
Sources gave no indication HuA threatens the US.
